extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (UK and international) considering or preparing applications to Royal Society grants and fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and high-level standards for applying to Royal Society funding schemes (e.g., fellowships and grants), including institutional eligibility, the types of research supported, and the principles that guide assessment and policy. Focused on prospective applicants and host institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles guiding funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work is guided by the principles of Excellence; Inclusivity; Flexibility; and Openness and Fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These core principles underpin the Royal Society's approach to funding, assessment and policy. Applications and award administration are expected to align with and be judged in light of these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusion expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society recognises that diversity is essential for delivering excellence in science, technology, engineering and mathematics, and wants to encourage applications from the widest range of backgrounds, perspectives and experiences to maximise innovation and creativity in science for the benefit of humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged from diverse backgrounds; selection and funding decisions seek to promote inclusivity to enhance innovation. Consideration of diversity is an explicit organisational priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Wolfson Fellowship host institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The five-year Royal Society Wolfson Fellowships enables UK universities and not-for-profit research institutions to attract and recruit talented…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied eligibility requirement: Wolfson Fellowships are targeted at UK universities and not-for-profit research institutions as hosts for the fellowship. Applicants should ensure host institution type matches scheme eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported research types
rubrics_metrics.description: We support scientists pursuing discovery-led and applied research through a wide range of schemes and career development opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding schemes prioritise either discovery-led or applied research (or both). Applicants should frame proposals as discovery-led and/or applied research consistent with scheme remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant calibre — outstanding researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships and grants for outstanding researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The portfolio is aimed at researchers who demonstrate high quality and excellence. Applicants should present evidence of strong research track-record and potential befitting an 'outstanding' researcher for the relevant scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant characteristics — freedom, support and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Royal Society funding provides freedom, support and flexibility to researchers in the UK and internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are intended to enable researchers to pursue their research with a degree of independence and adaptability. Applicants should consider how proposed work would benefit from this freedom and flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A step-by-step guide to the application and assessment process for our schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the published application and assessment process for each scheme. Detailed procedural guidance (forms, stages, assessment criteria) is available via the step-by-step guide linked on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application dates and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: See key dates for funding schemes, with open, close and decision dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must observe scheme-specific timelines (opening, closing and decision dates). Timely submission and awareness of deadlines are required; check the calendar for scheme-specific dates.
